newsitem.title: UK: COMMODITIES - Coffee slips, but traders wait on New York.
newsitem.headline: COMMODITIES - Coffee slips, but traders wait on New York.

text.p: London coffee prices eased on Monday but New York was shut for the President's Day holiday so traders said it was premature to call the end of a spectacular rally that has taken coffee up 50 percent since early January.

Arabica coffee futures traded in the New York market have set the pace in the rally by wholesale prices that has been based on a perception that stocks are low and that Brazil may have a smaller crop, as well as labour unrest in Colombia. The rally has led to rises on retail prices on ground coffee in Europe and the United States. London futures for the lower quality Robusta type of coffee rose as high as $1,705 per tonne on Friday but ended Monday down at $1,613 on the May contract.

The London market, which saw selling by origin countries and speculators, was reacting to a late Friday decline in New York where the direction may be influenced next by stocks data due on Tuesday from the US Green Coffee Association.

Markets will also keep an eye on current talks on allocating export quotas among central American members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries. Gold saw a London afternoon fixing at #344.10 per ounce which was just down from late traded values at the end of last week, but the bullion market was subdued by the US holiday.

Crude oil prices were also little changed with bellwether North Sea Brent Blend May futures easing to trade just above $20 per barrel, although ample supply is likely to continue to weigh on the market as winter fuel demand subsides.
Several industrial metals on the London Metal Exchange (LME) were slightly firmer, led by copper, in a move seen as largely technical.
"The market has seen copper hold at support over the past few trading days and it is probably taking some strength from that," said Martin Squires, analyst at Rudolf Wolff.
